title: Python Program Design
description: Connect functions, validation, return values, and a small main flow into code that is easy to test.

questions.prompt: What is a strong reason to split a program into small functions?
options: Each function can have one clear responsibility
It makes tests unnecessary
It guarantees every function is short
It keeps all state global
questions.correct: Each function can have one clear responsibility
questions.explanation: Small responsibilities make code easier to read, reuse, test, and diagnose.
The function adds 70 and 90, divides by 2, and returns the float 80.0.

questions.prompt: Pure functions are easier to test when the same inputs always produce the same outputs.
questions.explanation: A deterministic function has fewer hidden dependencies, so a test can check its contract directly.

questions.prompt: Where should interactive input usually be collected in a testable beginner program?
options: In main or a dedicated input function
Inside every helper so it stays near the calculation
At module import time
Inside tests only
questions.correct: In main or a dedicated input function
questions.explanation: Keeping interaction at the boundary lets the core functions accept arguments and return values to tests.
60 is greater than 59, so the Boolean function returns True.

questions.prompt: What should validation do before a calculation uses a grade?
options: Check that the value follows the allowed range
Convert it silently to any value
Let tests redefine the expected range
Run the calculation first and check afterward
questions.correct: Check that the value follows the allowed range
questions.explanation: Validation protects later calculations from values outside the assignment's contract.

questions.prompt: Printing a result and returning a result are interchangeable for an automated test.
questions.explanation: print displays text, while return supplies a value to the caller. Tests usually need the returned value.
Only F takes the failure branch; B reaches the final Pass return.

questions.prompt: Why is a main guard valuable in an assignment file?
options: Tests can import functions without starting the interactive program
It lets every file in the project run automatically
It turns input into integers
It suppresses exceptions from functions
questions.correct: Tests can import functions without starting the interactive program
questions.explanation: The guard separates importable definitions from the interactive command-line entry point.

questions.prompt: What is the best first check when a correct-looking submission gets a missing-function error?
options: Compare the required function name and parameters exactly
Reinstall Python before checking the name
Change the test's requested function
Run only the file interactively
questions.correct: Compare the required function name and parameters exactly
questions.explanation: Automated tests call the public names in the assignment contract, so spelling and signature are part of correctness.
